title: Perspectives and challenges in circularly polarized luminescence of lanthanide(III) complexes: From solution-based systems to solid-state applications
claim: For eight- and nine-coordinate Ln(III) complexes with square-antiprism or square-prism geometries, solution CPL is predicted to vanish at twist angles of 0°, 90°, and ±45° and to maximize near ±22.5°, following a sin(4θ) dependence.
explanation: Peacock’s correlation links the crystallographic twist about the principal axis to the angle between electric and magnetic dipoles. Conformational rigidity raises glum by fixing local helicity and the μ–m mixing, while more polarizable axial donors (water < ethanol < DMF < DMSO in the systems discussed) increase electric-dipole strength and lower glum.
scope: Chiral macrocyclic Ln(III) complexes of coordination numbers 8 and 9 in solution.
conditions: Square antiprism or square prism; θ is the twist angle of the principal axis.
caveats: A later Cs[Eu(hfbc)4] example has a torsion near −41.4°, close to the ideal SAP angle, yet very high glum, so twist angle alone does not explain every record value.
